message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | Key Points | |------|------------------------|------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Must be returned within 30 days after you move out (unless you give a written notice of intent to stay).
• Landlord may keep up to one month’s rent for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Landlord must provide an itemized list of deductions.
• If you dispute, you can file a claim in small‑claims court. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary condition.
• Repairs for plumbing, heating, electrical, structural issues, and pest control are required. | • Texas Property Code §92.001 requires landlords to keep premises in good repair. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑renewal or termination of a month‑to‑month lease: 30‑day written notice.
• For a fixed‑term lease: notice must be given before the lease expires. | • Written notice must be delivered personally or mailed. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice to pay rent or quit, 30‑day notice to vacate).
• If you fail to comply, the landlord can file an unlawful detainer action. | • Eviction is a judicial process; the landlord cannot forcibly remove you. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but it must be in writing and not violate any local ordinances. | • Some cities have rent‑control ordinances; check local laws. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | • Entry without notice can be a violation of your right to privacy. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • This is protected under the Fair Housing Act and Texas Property Code §92.001. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to fix major problems, you may repair them yourself and deduct the cost from rent (only if you follow proper procedure). | • Must give written notice to landlord first; keep receipts. | | **Lease Terms** | • All terms must be in writing.
• Oral agreements are enforceable but harder to prove. | • Ensure you receive a copy of the lease and any amendments. | | **Right to a Written Lease** | • Texas law requires a written lease for any tenancy longer than 30 days. | • The lease must include rent amount, due date, security deposit, and other essential terms. | | **Subletting** | • You may sublet only with landlord’s written consent (unless the lease prohibits it). | • Subletting without consent can be grounds for eviction. | | **Maintenance of Records** | • Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and notices. | • Useful if disputes arise. | --- #### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Make sure it includes all required disclosures (e.g., lead paint, mold, pest control). 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, and written records of any maintenance issues. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send all notices via certified mail or email with read receipt. 4. **Know Local Ordinances** – Some Texas cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas, Houston) have additional tenant protections. 5. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you face eviction or disputes, contact a local tenant‑rights organization or legal aid clinic. #### Resources | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** | Guides on landlord‑tenant disputes, complaint filing. | | **Texas Legal Services Center** | Free legal advice for low‑income tenants. | | **Local Tenant‑Rights Groups** | e.g., “Austin Tenants Union,” “Dallas Housing Advocacy.” | | **Small‑Claims Court** | For disputes over security deposits or unpaid rent. | | **Fair Housing Council of Texas** | Assistance with discrimination complaints. | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Moving In - [ ] Receive a written lease and confirm all terms. - [ ] Verify the landlord has provided required disclosures (lead paint, mold, etc.). - [ ] Inspect the unit and document any existing damage. - [ ] Confirm the security deposit amount and understand the return timeline. - [ ] Ask about the landlord’s policy on repairs and how to report issues. --- **Bottom Line:** As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, timely notice for any changes, protection against unlawful eviction, and the ability to seek legal recourse if your landlord violates the law. Stay informed, keep records, and don’t hesitate to seek help if you encounter problems.
